name: long_context
description: Long-context comprehension: a multi-section technical passage (~2k tokens) must be held and reasoned over. Stresses KV-cache growth, memory bandwidth and context handling.

workload.prompt:
Study the following release notes and answer the question at the end.

Section 1 - Scheduler: The runtime now batches prompt chunks before decode begins. Larger batches raise prompt-processing throughput but increase time-to-first-token slightly. A dynamic batch window adapts to queue depth.

Section 2 - Memory: KV-cache blocks are allocated per-sequence with copy-on-write sharing for common prefixes. Releasing a sequence returns blocks to a pool; fragmentation is reduced by compaction when the pool exceeds 80% utilization.

Section 3 - Quantization: K-quants moved to a per-block scales layout improving perplexity by roughly 1% at equal bitrate. V-cache may use a separate quantization type from K-cache.

Section 4 - Serving: Concurrent requests are multiplexed; throughput rises near-linearly until compute saturation, after which latency percentiles degrade faster than mean latency.

Question: In two sentences, summarize the trade-off between batching strategy and TTFT described in Section 1, and name one memory-management technique from Section 2.
